hook_text: A heavy stone with a dip in the middle. A metal iron with no plug. Can you guess what they were for?
clip_script: Mbombela, Mpumalanga. A Grade 4 class opens its own museum. A grinding stone, worn smooth by years of grinding maize. A flat iron, heated on the stove. A paraffin lamp. A coin from before South Africa used the rand. Each object is a clue. What is it made of? Who used it? What does it tell us? And at Mapungubwe, a tiny golden rhino eight hundred years old tells us about a whole kingdom. Objects speak, if we ask the right questions.
visual_style: Whiteboard table of mystery objects with question marks above them, each one turning to show a label and a tiny drawing of it being used.
mood: Playful guessing game that turns into discovery.
pacing: Mystery object, guess, reveal, then the questions to ask, ending with the golden rhino.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find one old object in your home to bring to class.
